name: tabular_anomaly_iforest
title: Unsupervised anomaly detection on machine telemetry: IsolationForest / OneClassSVM / LOF(novelty=True) fitted on the training window, contamination chosen on a validation split
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the unsupervised false-positive trap

forbidden.why: every fit in this file takes train_x, which the split at line 56 produced; the quantile transform is a Pipeline step of each detector, so it is refitted with the detector and never on its own

valid_x reaches detector.predict at line 96 only, and test_x reaches decision_function at lines 119-120 and predict at line 121; nothing is fitted on either. An unsupervised fit(X) with no y is still a fit on the TRAINING window here
there is no cross_val_score / cross_validate / *SearchCV call in this project at all; choose_contamination is a hand-rolled sweep that refits the whole Pipeline for every candidate
the telemetry columns are instantaneous readings; nothing parses a date, converts one or sorts by one, so there is no temporal signal for a random split to violate

f1_score is fed `flags` at lines 97 and 127, and both are produced by a `== -1` comparison followed by astype(int) - a decision, not a score. roc_auc_score and average_precision_score are score metrics and are correctly fed decision_function output
roc_auc_score at lines 123 and 126 is fed the negated decision_function, which is a continuous anomaly score - that is the documented correct argument, not a hard label
seed_everything() seeds random and numpy at lines 44-45, both splits carry random_state=SEED, and QuantileTransformer, IsolationForest and EllipticEnvelope each carry random_state=SEED
both train_test_split calls (lines 56 and 58) pass random_state=SEED
there is no torch in this project and no hand-written gradient step
model.eval() is a torch idiom with no sklearn equivalent
torch.no_grad() has no meaning in a scikit-learn program
no device is ever named in this project
nothing is pickled or loaded here

notes: This project exists to test the ROB-10 transformer guard from the other side. IsolationForest.fit, OneClassSVM.fit, LocalOutlierFactor.fit and EllipticEnvelope.fit are all bare .fit() calls on a feature matrix with no y at all, in a file that also contains two train_test_split calls - the exact surface MLV101 keys on. All four must stay silent because the receivers are detectors, not transformers, and because their argument is the training window.
